title: Visualización AR de Boceto de Almacén en Copenhague por Arquitecto Danés
prompt:
A Danish architect standing full-body near the edge of the frame, slightly to the left, in an unfinished Copenhagen waterfront warehouse space with exposed brick walls and bare concrete floors. The camera is positioned behind and slightly to the right of the person, capturing them from a three-quarter rear angle. The person stands calmly and thoughtfully, looking toward the space ahead.

The environment is raw and incomplete: empty industrial space with peeling paint, exposed steel beams, scattered construction materials, and large warehouse windows letting in cold Nordic light. The atmosphere feels quiet, austere, industrial, minimal, and full of potential. Natural daylight from the tall windows illuminates the scene, creating realistic shadows and depth with characteristic Scandinavian diffused light. Floating hand-drawn sketch lines appear over and within the environment, aligned precisely in perspective with the real space. These sketches represent a future sustainable mixed-use development with wooden elements and green spaces.

The sketch lines are black, clean, and hand-drawn, resembling architectural concept sketches made with pencil or technical pen. The strokes are expressive, slightly imperfect, and organic — not rigid or mechanical, showing influences of Danish modernist architecture. The sketched elements occupy the foreground and midground, appearing closer to the person than expected. Some sketch lines subtly overlap the person's silhouette and the real surfaces, visually merging imagination with reality. The sketches float naturally within the scene, seamlessly blending with the environment and conveying the idea of sustainable transformation and Nordic design philosophy coming to life.
